contracts.commit_point: The model-call wrap point: the request.override(tools=[], tool_choice='none') applied at backend/agents/middleware.py line 18 immediately before handler(request) at line 19 — i.e., before the model can emit any further dispatchable tool call. The guarded tool-invocation effect itself would commit at agent tool dispatch following the model response, which the emptied tool list prevents.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Custom ToolCallLimitMiddleware(AgentMiddleware) (backend/agents/middleware.py, lines 4-25): wrap_model_call computes tool_call_count from request.state['messages']; if count >= max_tool_calls it rewrites the request via request.override(tools=[], tool_choice='none') before returning handler(request); after_model additionally appends the SystemMessage 'Tool limit reached — answer now using only the data already gathered.' once the cap is reached. Instances are registered as the sole middleware in create_agent for both analyst nodes.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Any model call inside an agent run proceeding with tools available once the cumulative tool-call count in the agent state's message history has reached self.max_tool_calls (self.tool_call_count(state) >= self.max_tool_calls), and consequently any further agent tool call being dispatched or executed after the cap has been reached.

contracts.protection_obligation: Each analyst agent's tool calls executed through the create_agent tool loop (economist: Tavily/yfinance tools; fundamental_analyst: yfinance/screener tools) must be capped at the configured max_tool_calls per agent run (economist: max_tool_calls=3; fundamental_analyst: max_tool_calls=6) by registering a ToolCallLimitMiddleware instance in create_agent(middleware=[tool_limit_guard]); once the cap is reached, no further agent-dispatched tool call may occur because the middleware strips all tools and forces tool_choice='none' at the model-call wrap point. (Merged from the two duplicate reviewer opinions.)
scope_limits: backend/agents/economist.py line 64 calls get_company_profile.invoke({'ticker': ticker}) directly, outside the create_agent loop; ToolCallLimitMiddleware's hooks operate only on agent-run state, so this direct pre-loop tool invocation is NOT covered by the cap.

The cap is per agent run: each node invocation constructs a fresh agent with fresh message state (economist.py lines 57-78; fundamental_analyst.py lines 58-75), so the count resets on every run even though tool_limit_guard is a shared module-level instance.
